entities.name: Diarmait mac Maíl na mBó
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Diarmait mac Máel na mBó was a paramount king in Ireland during the pre-Norman era, ruling Leinster and as High King of Ireland. His reign spanned from 1014 to 1072, with his capital in Dublin. He played a pivotal role in shaping Irish politics and society, fostering cultural exchange with neighboring kingdoms.

Mac Máel na mBó's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he contributed to the preservation of Irish language and literature. His reign also saw significant military victories, particularly against the Vikings, securing Ireland's borders.

Despite his many achievements, Mac Máel na mBó's later years were marked by conflict with other kingdoms, ultimately leading to his downfall. His legacy, however, continues to be celebrated in Irish history and culture.

The 12th-century manuscript 'Annals of the Four Masters' records Diarmait mac Máel na mBó as a king who 'slew many men and was slain by the sons of Donal'.
